This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder. Campaigning in Kansas last night,
President Trump said Democrats want to make the U.S. more like France,
which has experienced days of rioting leading to curfews in parts of Paris and other major cities.
If you want to see what is at stake in this election,
just look at what's happening in France, a once great nation
that is being conquered, looted, and burned to the ground.
Kansas was Trump's latest stop in a campaign blitz heading into the November midterm elections
as Republican candidates face voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices.
Voters here have not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in more than 90 years,
but first-term Senator Roger Marshall is in a tight race with his Democratic opponent,
Adam Hamilton, a pastor of a Methodist megachurch.
The protests in France began as a strike by high school students in Paris.
They've since ballooned into violent nationwide protests over schools
and the cost of living that Trump himself has struggled to contain.
Temporary protected status was set to expire Monday,
but now being extended for people from Ukraine and Sudan.
NPR's Jasmine Garse reports it's unclear, though, how long those protections will remain in effect.
Temporary protected status, or TPS, grants temporary lawful residents work authorization
and protection from deportation to certain foreigners.
Tens of thousands of Ukrainians and hundreds of Sudanese immigrants living in the U.S. have it.
In a statement, Homeland Security said a decision on both countries will be, quote,
"made at the appropriate time."
Until then, the agency added that Ukrainians and Sudanese
who are enrolled in the program will retain protection.
Over the last year and a half, the Trump administration has terminated TPS for
more than one million people from over a dozen countries,
including Afghanistan, Haiti and Venezuela.
Jasmine Garse, NPR News, Washington.
Commercial goods could soon start entering Gaza again
days after a handful of powerful Palestinian merchants suspended imports
in a dispute with Hamas over collecting taxes.
NPR's Anas Baba reports from Gaza.
The price of food has skyrocketed in Gaza,
as some items like eggs and fresh vegetables became harder to find.
It came after a strike by private sector merchants protesting what they said
were pain in demands and threats from Hamas.
Now Israel's agency, Kogat, says the merchants say Hamas has withdrawn its demands
and commercial shipments will resume gradually.
But even if the flow of commercial goods resumes,
it could take time for supplies to reach markets and prices to come down.
It comes as the UN World Food Programme says.
Funding shortage have forced it to cut food assistance to half a million people in Gaza.
Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
This is NPR News.
Canadian media are projecting that voters in Alberta have rejected a referendum
on moving toward independence.
With more than 1.3 million votes counted so far,
the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation says 76 percent supported remaining in Canada,
compared with 23 percent who backed beginning the process that could lead to separation.
The man who attacked demonstrators in Boulder last summer
has reached a plea agreement in his federal hate crimes case,
Grace Dorflora, Member Station KUNC,
reports this could resolve the remaining federal charges against him and avoid a trial.
Court documents show the details of Mohammed Sabry Soleiman's plea agreement
will be made public during a hearing on October 29th.
Soleiman has also withdrawn requests to stop his family from being deported
to comply with the plea agreement.
The federal charges stem from his attack last June on Boulder's Pearl Street,
where one woman was killed and several others were injured.
They were demonstrating in support of Israeli hostages in Gaza.
Soleiman is already serving a life sentence
after pleading guilty to a slew of state charges.
For NPR News, I'm Grace Dorflora in Denver.
Major League Baseball's World Series is set.
The Tampa Bay Rays will play the Milwaukee Brewers in a matchup of teams that have never won the title.
Tampa Bay advanced last night with a 7-3 game six victory over the Cleveland Guardians.
World Series begins on Friday.
The WNBA Finals now tied at a game of peace see Atlanta Dream beat Golden State's 79-65 last night.
This is NPR News.

Commercial goods may resume entering Gaza after merchants suspended imports over Hamas tax dispute
Canadian media project Alberta voters reject referendum on moving toward independence
Man who attacked Boulder demonstrators reaches federal hate crimes plea agreement, hearing set October 29
Tampa Bay Rays beat Cleveland Guardians 7-3 to face Milwaukee Brewers in World Series
Atlanta Dream beat Golden State Valkyries 79-65, tying WNBA Finals at one game apiece
